reader.requirement: Within one Procedure Division a file-name may be named in at most one USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION/ERROR statement (ERROR and EXCEPTION are synonyms, SR4): a second USE statement naming it is refused, while one statement writing it twice, a mode-scoped USE (INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND) that also covers it, a USE FOR DEBUGGING naming it, and a contained program's own USE on the same GLOBAL file (a different Procedure Division) are legal; this holds for sequential, relative and indexed files alike.
reader.edition-search: Read DeclBindUse's file-name arm (_useFiles.Register -> Duplicate -> COBOL0897), DeclEndUseStatement, the per-builder register fields (one ProcedureTableBuilder per bound unit, reset per method), ConstructOperandRegister; grepped ConstructOperandRegister.cs and the DeclBindUse region for Edition|Year|CobolVersion: none. The USE GLOBAL / Format 3 gates of VersionConformancePass concern other phrases.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1_use_sr8_file_named_twice is the accepting half (one statement naming F1 twice, sequential files); the refusal across two statements, relative/indexed files, mode-scoped overlap, the debugging USE and the nested-program Procedure Division boundary are not witnessed at 85

probes.printed: error COBOL0897: declarative section 'D2': file 'RELF' already has a USE procedure in this procedure division (ISO §2023:14.9.49.3 SR8)
probes.expected: refused: RELF (relative) named in USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION and in a second USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR statement

probes.expected: legal: outer and contained program each have their own USE on the GLOBAL relative file GRF; each program's duplicate-key WRITE invokes its own declarative (VIII.4.8.4 GR1)

probes.printed: D1 ST=22 ST2=?? / AFTER DUP ST=22 / D1 ST=00 ST2=35 / AFTER OPEN ST2=35
probes.expected: legal: indexed IXF and sequential SQF named in one USE while USE ON INPUT and ON I-O also exist; the file-name USE takes precedence for both (GR4, GR5b), D2 never runs

probes.expected: legal at 85: USE FOR DEBUGGING ON RELF (a 1985-only form) is not a USE AFTER EXCEPTION statement, so naming RELF in it and in one USE AFTER EXCEPTION is not a repeat

probes.printed: COBOL0307 unexpected 'RELF' (INPUT and a file-name in one USE)
probes.expected: refused by the general format (one brace alternative per statement); degenerate form

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.3 SR3  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3

reader.notes: The 1985 SR3 as amended by X3.23b-1993 is the same rule as 2023's SR8, and the compiler applies one register keyed by file-name, closed per USE statement and reset per Procedure Division. usesr3a draws the same COBOL0897 at --std 2023. The diagnostic cites only the 2023 clause.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VIII.4.8.3 SR3 (as amended by X3.23b-1993), SR4, GR4, §1985:X.5.5.2 (USE [GLOBAL] AFTER). ProcedureTableBuilder.cs#DeclBindUse keys _useFiles by fn.GetText() with CobolNames.Comparer, reset per Procedure Division. Probes at 85: rsr3a - USE ... ON RELF and a second USE ... ON relf (lowercase): refused 'COBOL0897: declarative section D2: file relf already has a USE procedure in this procedure division'. rsr3b - USE GLOBAL AFTER ... ON RELF and a plain USE AFTER ... ON RELF in the same Procedure Division (1985 IPC form): refused COBOL0897. rsr2c - the 2002 Format 3 file form is refused at 85 (COBOL0877), so it cannot enter the register. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.3 SR3  (4.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'.
